newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Higher air cargo rates not due to yield - BA.
newsitem.headline: Higher air cargo rates not due to yield - BA.

text.p: British Airways is confident the October 1 rise in London-bound air cargo rates need not be met by strong objections from the market and that it has nothing to do with low yields, a BA spokeswoman told Reuters.

BA is one of the major air cargo carriers flying from Hong Kong to Europe which have informally agreed to raise rates by HK$2 per kg from October 1. That increase follows a similarly imposed HK$3 per kg rise in August.

"The rise is an adjustment to market supply and demand and has nothing whatsoever to do with low yield. Over the past 12 months British Airways has lowered its price and right now is making up for that price reduction when the rate has dropped by 10-20 percent," she said.

"With the recent rise in the air cargo rate in August, the rate is now closer to the level of what it was 10 months ago but is still 10 percent down. The market response for the August price rise has been accepted as we think the October rise will be," she added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
